title: GraphAccel: An In-Storage Accelerator for Efficient Graph-Based Vector Similarity Search Using Page Packing and Speculative Search Optimization
problem: Graph-based approximate vector similarity search (essential for retrieval-augmented generation and AI applications) often stores large-scale graphs on SSDs, but SSD page access patterns and latency underutilize available bandwidth and compute resources.
motivation: Accelerating graph-based vector search on SSDs is critical for efficient retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and other AI applications that require fast nearest-neighbor search at scale.
method: GraphAccel is specialized hardware built into SSDs that speeds up vector similarity searches—finding similar numerical representations (like embeddings for text or images) by navigating a graph (network of connected nodes). It works two ways: first, it physically groups related nodes together on disk so queries require fewer storage page reads; second, it predicts which data paths you'll explore next and fetches them in advance, while the SSD's idle processing channels simultaneously work on multiple search paths. Results are compared against existing approaches like DiskANN and DiskANN++.
key_novelty: GraphAccel puts specialized hardware inside SSDs for faster vector similarity searches by keeping related graph nodes close together and fetching likely future data before it's requested.
contributions: In-storage accelerator architecture for graph-based vector similarity search
Page packing optimization reducing SSD page accesses per query
Speculative search scheme maximizing idle SSD chip/channel utilization
Performance improvements over DiskANN and DiskANN++
primary_theme: In-storage acceleration for SSD-based graph vector search
